Issued at 229 PM CDT Sun Jul 19 2026

A few light showers persist across the area this afternoon. These 
showers are also accompanied by a mid level cloud deck which has 
kept temperatures a bit cooler than previously expected. However, 
sunshine remains across parts of south central South Dakota. Thus, 
temperatures have warmed to the upper 70s, 80s, and a few locations 
pushing into the 90s. With dew points remaining in the 60s to low 
70s, heat indices have warmed to the 80s and 90s with a few 
locations hitting 100F. With some diurnal warming left to go, should 
still see the heat indices nudge a little higher, allowing for the 
Heat Advisory to remain in effect until 9PM this evening. Another 
round of showers and thunderstorms remains possible late tonight 
into tomorrow morning (11PM to 6AM). These storms will develop along 
a cold front in North Dakota and move southeastwards through the 
evening hours. These storms may grow into a line as they push 
southeastwards. However, there remains some uncertainty in whether 
these storms will push into southwest Minnesota or stay just outside 
the forecast area. These storms look to be focused on the nose of 
the low level jet where convergence and the strongest warm air 
advection (WAA) will lie. The bulk of the hi-res guidance and the 
ensembles also support the storms remaining in this location. Still 
have left light chance to chance PoPs across southwest Minnesota in 
case lingering showers and storms pass through the area.

The thermal ridge will push directly over the forecast area on 
Monday, pushing 850 mb temperatures up to +25C to about +30C. Mixing 
these temperatures down to the surface will result in widespread 
high temperatures up to the 90s to low 100s, hottest along the 
Missouri River Valley. With dew points remaining in the 60s to low 
70s, heat indices will warm up to 100F to 105F south of I-90. As 
such, have issued another Heat Advisory for this area. The Advisory 
is in effect from noon to 8 pm. The previously mentioned cold front 
will be pushing through the area throughout the day. While this 
front will cool temperatures, the main cold advective push from the 
front will come in the late afternoon and evening timeframe, thus 
allowing for hot and humid conditions to continue. This front will 
serve as the focal point for additional showers and storms between 
4PM and 10PM. The front will push through rather quickly, limiting 
the severe weather threat to near and south of highway-20. Storms 
look to remain more discrete as the develop and quickly race out of 
the area along the boundary. The moisture pooling along the boundary 
will push CAPE values up to 2,000 to 2,500 J/kg. Hodographs show 
deep layer shear values on the order of about 45 knots. Hodographs 
are generally straight with slight backing aloft. This should allow 
for large hail up to the size of golf balls. DCAPE will also be high 
around 1,500 J/kg, resulting in the potential for damaging winds to 
70 mph. Since these storms are discrete and look to only impact a 
small area, should only see isolated impacts from severe storms. 
Once the front pushes through, temperatures will fall to the 60s to 
low 70s overnight.

Tuesday will be a cooler day with the post frontal airmass in place. 
High temperatures will be seasonable in the 80s with dew points 
falling to the 50s. While this would usually make for a pleasant 
Summer day, smoke will filter in behind the front which could affect 
sensitive individuals. Fortunately, it looks like the highest 
concentration of smoke will come Monday night into Tuesday morning 
and be slowly decreased thereafter. These seasonable conditions will 
persist for the rest of the work week as northwest flow persists 
aloft. Next chances for rain look to come on Thursday and Friday as 
a shortwave trough pushes through the area. The ensembles support 
this as they show a 40-60% chance for rainfall amounts exceeding a 
tenth of an inch for this period of time. Instability looks to be 
quite limited, so severe storms are not expected at this time. Upper 
level ridging looks to potentially make a comeback next weekend, 
leading to a return of above average temperatures. This potential 
remains uncertain so will keep an eye on how the pattern evolves 
over the next week.
